matchups.analysis: Rob's sitting at 5% because he's already done—126.9 is his final score, and Veton's projected to 140.2 with Charbonnet and Kupp still waiting to play, which means this is basically a formality at this point. Jayden Daniels dropping a pathetic 15.0 when he was supposed to sling for 22.8 didn't help, but that's not even the real problem—the real problem is Rob's entire team decided this was the week to show up exactly as expected or worse, while Veton's already got Tony Pollard's 27.2 destroying his 13.8 projection sitting in the bank and two legitimate studs still on the clock. Rob didn't make a meaningful lineup mistake, which is almost worse because it means his roster just sucks relative to Veton's, and no amount of lineup creativity was gonna bridge a gap this wide when you're looking at a 13-point projected deficit with no one left to play.

Faton's sitting pretty at 76% with ESPN projecting a 30-point blowout (108.2 to 97.8), and Ben's already completely cooked because his entire roster decided to clock out after halftime—Joe Burrow threw his ass 39.5 points early and then apparently everyone else got the memo that this matchup was over. But here's the thing that actually matters: Ben's got zero starters left to sweat while Faton's still got D'Andre Swift, Colston Loveland, and Rome Odunze waiting, which means Faton could legitimately blow this despite sitting on a 30-point cushion if he decides to bench his good players again like he did with Wan'Dale Robinson (12.7 pts on the bench while Drake London got a full day to disappoint him for 1.3), so Ben's got at least a small prayer that Faton finds new and creative ways to sabotage himself. The real problem for Ben is that he benched DeMario Douglas (15.1) to roll the dice on KC Concepcion (5.2)—that 9.9-point swing would've tightened this considerably if he'd just not done that, but as constructed right now Faton's got the win locked down barring a legitimate collapse, and even with his history of roster mismanagement this gap's too fat to blow. Ben had a chance to make this interesting if he'd managed his bench like a functional adult, but instead he's gonna watch Faton cruise home while holding regrets about the points he left sitting on his bench.

Nori's sitting pretty at 98% with ESPN projecting him to 101.0 while Ilir's limping toward 94.9—a 6-point projected gap that turns into a complete autopsy when Ilir's got exactly one guy left to play and needs the Seahawks D/ST to somehow score like a playoff defense while Nori's already got the game locked down with all his starters in the books. The real damage isn't even the Seahawks lottery ticket—it's that Bijan Robinson absolutely shit the bed (7.6 when he was supposed to give you 18.2), and Ilir's entire remaining path depends on him getting 6+ points from a defense that's averaging 5.1 on the season, which is basically asking for a miracle when you're already betting against your own roster's setup. Nori's got the win wrapped up despite benching Jacoby Brissett in favor of Jared Goff costing him 5.6 points—he's got enough cushion that even a stupid lineup decision doesn't matter, which is the kind of comfortable position you build when your depth actually cooperates instead of imploding like Ilir's did. This one's over.

Jetmir's staring down a 23-point projected loss (87.2 to 110.3) with a 1% win probability, which is basically ESPN saying this is done before Luther Burden even takes the field—and honestly, they're right when Arben's already got Chuba Hubbard printing 21.4 points against his 14.0 projection while sitting on Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Trey McBride still waiting to clock in. But the real murder weapon here is Jetmir's lineup construction: benching Tyler Allgeier (33.6 fucking points) to start Ollie Gordon II (6.9) cost him 26.7 points—that's not a close call, that's the entire ballgame right there, that's the difference between making this respectable and getting absolutely torched. Kenneth Walker coming in at 10.4 against his 18.4 projection just adds insult to injury when your depth is already getting exposed, and even if Luther Burden goes nuclear, Jetmir's entire remaining roster would need to hit ceiling simultaneously while Arben's just coasting on studs already proving they show up—this one's over before the night window even starts.

Rilind's sitting at 54% win probability with ESPN projecting a 5.6-point win (99.4 to 93.5), but he's about to get absolutely torched by his own lineup decisions—benching Ryan Flournoy for Ja'Kobi Lane cost him nearly 10 points, and that's the kind of self-inflicted wound that'll haunt him when this comes down to the wire. Flamur's already locked in 99.1 with nobody left to play, which means Rilind needs Bears D/ST to go nuclear while he's also trying to overcome the fact that he benched the right guy and started the wrong one in the same slot like he was deliberately sabotaging himself. Matthew Stafford throwing up a dud (8.3 when he was supposed to be 17.0) isn't helping either, but the real story here is that Rilind had Flournoy sitting on the bench scoring 11.6 points and chose violence instead—that's not bad luck, that's bad decision-making at the worst possible time. Flamur's Chris Godwin Jr. special (0.0 pts) is somehow worse on paper, but he's already got his points in the vault and doesn't need another miracle, while Rilind's sitting here needing to overcome his own stupidity plus whatever the Bears are about to do on a cold December night.

Adam's sitting at 88.8 with absolutely nothing left to play, and ESPN's essentially called this a funeral—he's staring at a 3-point projected loss to Rinor's 91.7 because his entire Sunday already went sideways the second he benched Dylan Sampson (9.9 pts) to start Tyler Higbee (1.9 pts), which is an 8-point swing that basically became the entire ballgame. Zay Flowers decided to put up a fat goose egg after projecting for 16.7, which is the cherry on top of a lineup decision that's gonna haunt him all week, but honestly the real killer is that he didn't have the guts to trust his own bench depth when it actually mattered. Rinor's locked in at 91.7 with no meaningful mistakes and his remaining guys (Henry, Metcalf, Prescott) are just filling out a victory that's already mathematically guaranteed—this one's done.

Rob's sitting pretty at 51% with a microscopic 2.3-point projected edge, but he's starting from actual zero while Veton's already locked in 20.2 from Josh Jacobs absolutely demolishing his 13.6 projection—that head start is way heavier than ESPN's win probability math wants to admit when both guys are running nine starters left to play. Rob's got the ceiling weaponry (Rice, Wilson, Williams could theoretically all explode), but he's essentially asking three elite receivers to cooperate at the exact same time while Veton just needs Chase to show up and maybe ride some Tony Pollard action if the game gets into a grinding script—that's a completely different assignment. The fact that neither guy torpedoed their lineup in a meaningful way keeps this live through the late window, but Veton's got the insurance policy already cashed while Rob's entire path depends on everything breaking exactly right simultaneously, which is a much harder ask even when the projection says it's basically a coin flip.

Faton's cruising at 58% with a 12.9-point projected edge, but both of y'all are sitting at dead zero and he's still got nine starters waiting to play—the problem is he's built his entire path to victory on needing James Cook, Drake London, D'Andre Swift, and Rome Odunze to all show up and cooperate simultaneously, which is basically asking his bench depth to execute in perfect sync while Ben's just waiting for Travis Kelce and Justin Jefferson to literally exist and be elite. Ben's got way more margin for error here because his two studs are more reliable than Faton needing four separate cogs all spinning at the right RPM, and ESPN's essentially saying Faton wins if his depth cooperates and Ben loses if his all-world talents underperform—that's a completely different bet. This stays live through the night window since neither guy fucked up their lineup, but Faton should be sweating the fact that his 13-point cushion depends on his entire bench hitting their marks while Ben's just banking on his two best players doing what they're built for, and history says that's the smarter wager when you're down to the wire.

Nori's cruising at 53% with ESPN projecting a 5-point win (105.9 to 100.9), and that's basically what it looks like when one team actually built depth that executes while the other one's banking on eight different guys all deciding to go nuclear simultaneously just to stay competitive. Ilir's got the ceiling plays technically—Josh Allen, Bijan Robinson, George Pickens all still waiting—but ESPN's math is saying those three would need to combine for a perfect game while Nori's just sitting back waiting for Jahmyr Gibbs, Breece Hall, and Brock Bowers to literally just be the players they're supposed to be, and that's a completely different assignment. The fact that Jalen Coker already underperformed isn't even the real problem; the real problem is Ilir built a roster where one dud cascades into needing everyone else to overdeliver, while Nori's got enough depth that he can lose one guy and still win comfortably. This stays technically live through the night window since Ilir's holding legitimate weapons, but Nori's got the projected edge, the win probability, and a roster construction that doesn't require miracles—Ilir needs everything to break exactly right at once, and that's just not the bet you want to be riding on when you're already trailing.

Jetmir's sitting at 37% because ESPN's basically already called this a funeral—he's staring at a 20.8-point projected deficit (104.5 to 125.3) with Kenneth Walker, Rhamondre Stevenson, and Luther Burden as his hope chest, while Arben's got Jonathan Taylor, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Trey McBride still waiting to punch the clock. Tetairoa McMillan already shit the bed by 4.1 points, which would sting less if Jetmir had built literally any depth redundancy instead of rolling the dice on role players and lottery tickets—he's basically praying for a miracle week while Arben's just waiting for his studs to show up and be studs. Kyler Murray and Hunter Henry would both need to absolutely explode just to make this respectable, and even then Jetmir's still asking his entire remaining bench to hit ceiling simultaneously while Arben's got production already locked in from Chuba (21.4 pts, crushed his 14.0 projection) and everything else is just gravy. This one's over before the night window unless Jetmir's remaining guys decide to collectively go nuclear, which ain't the math you want to ride on down 21.

Flamur's walking out of here at 57% with ESPN projecting a 12.5-point blowout (109.3 to 96.8), and that gap is basically the entire ballgame when both teams are sitting at absolute zero with nine starters left to play. Flamur's got CeeDee Lamb, Saquon Barkley, and Tee Higgins just waiting to clock in and be their elite selves, while Rilind's entire path to victory requires Amon-Ra St. Brown, Ashton Jeanty, Harold Fannin Jr., and Rico Dowdle to all somehow decide this is the week they go absolutely nuclear—that's not a comeback strategy, that's wishful thinking. Rilind's got the runway technically with nine guys still out there, but ESPN's essentially saying he needs ceiling games across his entire remaining bench just to sniff this while Flamur's three studs are basically locks to execute their jobs, and that's a completely different assignment when you're chasing 13 points with complementary pieces and backup running backs. Flamur should cruise home here unless Rilind's entire remaining roster decides to go haywire simultaneously, which ain't the math you want to ride on when you're already down double digits before any meaningful production hits the board.

Rinor's sitting at 53% with ESPN projecting a clean 5.4-point win (117.4 to 112.0), and Adam's gonna need his entire remaining eight-man roster to execute in perfect sync just to stay competitive—Drake Maye, Puka Nacua, Khalil Shakir, and Zay Flowers all need to hit their marks simultaneously while Rinor's just waiting for Derrick Henry, DK Metcalf, and Dak Prescott to show up as late-window chalk and do exactly what they're supposed to do. Tucker Kraft overperforming by 5.7 points is solid, but it's already baked into Adam's score and doesn't change the fact that Matthew Golden already outperformed his projection by 4.6—Rinor's depth is already proving it shows up while Adam's is still hoping. This stays live through the late window since Adam's got legitimate ceiling plays, but Rinor's got the better remaining roster construction, the projected edge, and the win probability, which means Adam needs everything to break exactly right just to sniff this one. Rinor cruises home unless Adam's entire bench decides to go absolutely nuclear at the same time.
